title: Sharp bounds for perfect quantum state classification beyond antidistinguishability
summary: A multiset of pure quantum states is said to be k-learnable if there is a measurement strategy that always narrows an unknown sample drawn from the list down to one of at most k candidates. The parameter k interpolates between distinguishability and antidistinguishability, and provides a unified framework for partial state identification. We prove two universal, and optimal, Gram-matrix criteria for k-learnability: a Frobenius-norm sufficient condition and an entrywise-$\ell_1$ necessary condition.
